concepts.label: ip-vpn
concepts.gloss: An ip-vpn (L3VPN) is the customer Layer‑3 VPN service as seen by the provider, which is realized in the network by creating one or more per-device routing-instances (VRFs) for that customer.
concepts.example: vpn ACME is an ip-vpn service that is implemented by the VRFs vrf ACME@R-PE1, vrf ACME@R-PE2 and vrf ACME@R-PE3 on the provider edge devices.

concepts.label: routing-instance
concepts.gloss: A routing-instance (VRF) is the per-device routing table and associated configuration that isolates a single customer VPN's routes and policies on a specific provider edge device.
concepts.example: vrf ACME@R-PE1 is the VRF for the ACME VPN running on device R-PE1 and contains that device's view of ACME routes, interfaces and policies.

concepts.label: attachment-circuit
concepts.gloss: An attachment-circuit (sub-interface) is the physical or logical interface on a PE that is bound into a VRF to carry a CE's traffic into that routing-instance.
concepts.example: ge-0/0/1.101 is an attachment-circuit bound into vrf ACME@R-PE1 and provides the PE side of the link to the CE for the ACME service.

concepts.label: ce-device
concepts.gloss: A ce-device (customer edge) is the customer's router that sits across an attachment-circuit and peers with the provider edge to exchange reachability for the VPN.
concepts.example: CE-A router is the customer edge device connected across ge-0/0/1.101 and peers with R-PE1 to carry ACME routes into the provider network.

concepts.label: rd
concepts.gloss: A route-distinguisher (RD) is the per‑VRF identifier applied to routes on a VRF (typically per device) to make otherwise overlapping customer IPv4 prefixes unique in the provider's VPN address space.
concepts.example: 65000:101 is the RD assigned under vrf ACME@R-PE1 to distinguish ACME prefixes advertised from R-PE1 in the VPN.

concepts.label: route-target
concepts.gloss: A route-target (RT) is a BGP extended community value attached to a VRF that encodes the import/export policy for VPN routes (i.e., which VRFs will import routes exported by this VRF).
concepts.example: target 65000:1 (hub) is configured under vrf ACME@R-PE1 to export ACME routes to VRFs that import the 65000:1 community (hub role).

concepts.label: interface-address
concepts.gloss: An interface-address is the IP prefix assigned to an attachment-circuit that serves as the PE endpoint address for the PE–CE adjacency.
concepts.example: 10.0.1.1/30 is the interface-address configured on ge-0/0/1.101 facing CE-A (for example CE-A 10.0.1.2/30) on vrf ACME@R-PE1.

concepts.label: service-policy
concepts.gloss: A service-policy (QoS policy) is a traffic-handling policy (e.g., policing, shaping, queuing) that is attached to an attachment-circuit to enforce bandwidth and priority for a customer's traffic into a VRF.
concepts.example: policy-map gold-200M is a service-policy attached to ge-0/0/1.101 to guarantee up to 200 Mbps of gold-class service for ACME on R-PE1.

concepts.label: device
concepts.gloss: A device is a provider edge router node that carries one or more VRFs, attachment-circuits and BGP sessions to implement IP‑VPN services.
concepts.example: R-PE1 is a device that carries vrf ACME@R-PE1 and hosts interfaces like ge-0/0/1.101 and iBGP sessions to other PEs.

concepts.label: ce-protocol
concepts.gloss: A ce-protocol is the routing protocol configuration (PE‑to‑CE) applied on an attachment-circuit to exchange routes with the customer edge device for a VRF.
concepts.example: eBGP to CE-A is the CE protocol configured on ge-0/0/1.101 so R-PE1 and CE-A exchange ACME prefixes via eBGP for vrf ACME@R-PE1.

concepts.label: route-map
concepts.gloss: A route-map (routing-policy) is a routing policy applied under a VRF to filter or transform routes as they are imported into or exported from that VRF.
concepts.example: route-map ACME-in is applied under vrf ACME@R-PE1 to match and modify incoming CE routes before they are placed into the ACME VRF.

concepts.label: bgp-neighbor
concepts.gloss: A bgp-neighbor (iBGP session) is the internal BGP peer relationship on a provider edge device used to exchange VPN (e.g., VPNv4/VPNv6) routes with other PEs.
concepts.example: ibgp to R-PE2 is the iBGP neighbor configured on R-PE1 that carries ACME VPN routes from R-PE1 to R-PE2.

concepts.label: vrf-tag-0x7
concepts.gloss: vrf-tag-0x7 is a vendor‑specific opaque VRF tag or identifier attached under a VRF for proprietary forwarding or feature behavior and has no standard semantics outside that vendor's implementation.
concepts.example: vrf-tag-0x7 on vrf ACME@R-PE1 is a proprietary tag assigned by the device OS to the ACME VRF on R-PE1 for internal handling.
